page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at top left. Two engraved medallions with rim legends side by side, centred above the text. Below them one block of running text in two paragraphs, full width. No margin notes, no catchword or signature.

main_text.l: P. M.
CLEMENS VII
ODET DE FOIX
S DE LAL[?]
CLEMENS, huius nóminis Papa feptimus, Adriano fu-
pradicto in Pontificatu succeffit anno mundi 5484. à Christo
nato 1522. Hic antea Iulius vocabatur, sed Cardinalium quo-
rundam fuafu, Clementis nomen assumpsit. Fuit Leo decimus
huic patruelis. Dicitur Clemens fauisse Francorum Regi Fran-
cisco etiam capto, aduerfus Cæsarem Carolu: ideoq; Romā ab
exercitu Cæsaris, cui præerat Carolus Borbonius, direptā ac ex-
pilatam, nihilominus tamen ab hoc coronā accepit Carolus im-
perialem, præterea sacram vnctionem: fuit rarissimi ac callidissi-
mi ingenij. Frācisci Valesij partes iterum secutus, ad Massiliam
cum eo conuenit, initúmque est marrimoniū[?] proneptis fuæ Ca-
tharinæ Laurentij Medices Ducis Vrbinatis filiæ, cum Henrico
Duce Aurelianensi, nunc autem Francorum Rege. Florētiam
vrbem patriam obsedit, quā post annum obsidionis cepit: Du-
cémque in ea constituit Alexādrū Medices, prædicti Laurentij
Medices filium naturalem. Aiunt prouocatum à Florentinis id
bellum gessisse, qui in cognatos ac necessarios huius Clemen-
tis infesti essent, atque etiā in ipsum Pontificem infensi: vitio ta-
men illi interim vertitur, quôd in patriam ita fæuierit, quam
etiam velut sub iugum miserit: fedit annis 12. Vide Iouium, Sup-
plem. Chro. & Platinam.
ODETVS de Foix, dictus Lautretius, Mediolani sub Fran-
cisco Valesio praefectus, deinde exercitus Gallici in Italia
Dux, Papiā & Alexandriā expugnauit: Neapolim exercitu duxit: quô
dū tederet Clementi, quē Aurafiensis Princeps sub custodia tene-
bat, opē attulit: Porrò vbi Neapolim peruenit, arridētis fortunæ
occasione captare nesciuit: nā cominus si vrbē aggressus esset,
hāc facilè cepisset: sed interim dū eminus nimis cūctatur, Nea-
polis auxiliares Hispanos milites recipit: tandē tum ob aeris in-
temperantiam, tum ob aquas veneno infectas cum multis aliis
Gallorū primoribus periit an. D. 1528. Vide Suppl. & Iouium.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions above the text, with rim legends transcribed above; the legend at the lower left of the right medallion is partly cut off, so "S DE LAL" is doubtful. Doubtful readings: "marrimoniū" (type broken at the word, likely matrimonium). The text is set in roman type with macrons and some ligatures (ff, ss), all rendered with plain s. No marginal notes.
